entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 3 Zep 3:1-20 . Resumption of the Denunciation of Jerusalem, as Being Unreformed by the Punishment of Other Nations: After Her Chastisement Jehovah Will Interpose for Her against Her Foes; His Worship Shall Flourish in All Lands, Beginning at Jerusalem, Where He Shall Be in the Midst of His People, and Shall Make Them a Praise in All the Earth. 1. filthy-- Maurer translates from a different root, "rebellious," "contumacious." But the following term, "polluted," refers rather to her inward moral filth, in spite of her outward ceremonial purity [Calvin]. Grotius says, the Hebrew is used of women who have prostituted their virtue. There is in the Hebrew Moreah; a play on the name Moriah, the hill on which the temple was built; implying the glaring contrast between their filthiness and the holiness of the worship on Moriah in which they professed to have a share. oppressing-- namely, the poor, weak, widows, orphans and strangers ( Jr 22:3 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12962"/><div sID="gen24290" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12962"/><hi type="bold">8. wait ye upon me--</hi>Here Jehovah turns to the pious Jews. Amidst all these judgments on the Jewish nation, look forward to the glorious time of restoration to be ushered in by God's precious outpouring of wrath on all nations, <reference osisRef="Isa.30.18-Isa.30.33">Is 30:18-33</reference>; where the same phrase, "blessed are all they that wait for Him," is used as to the same great event. Calvin erroneously makes this verse an address to the ungodly; and so Maurer, "Ye shall not have to wait for Me in vain"; I will presently come armed with indignation: I will no longer contend with you by My prophets.<div eID="gen24290" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24291" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">until the day--</hi>that is, waiting for the day (<reference osisRef="Hab.2.3">Ha 2:3</reference>).<div eID="gen24291" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24292" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rise up to the prey--</hi>like a savage beast rising from his lair, greedy for the prey (compare <reference osisRef="Matt.24.28">Mt 24:28</reference>). Or rather, as a warrior leading Israel to certain victory, which is expressed by "the prey," or booty, which is the reward of victory. The Septuagint and Syriac versions read the Hebrew, "I rise up as a witness" (compare <reference osisRef="Job.16.8">Job 16:8</reference>; Mal 3:5). Jehovah being in this view witness, accuser, and judge. English Version is better (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.33.23">Is 33:23</reference>).<div eID="gen24292" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24293" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">gather the nations--</hi>against Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="Zech.14.2">Zec 14:2</reference>), to pour out His indignation upon them there (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.2">Joe 3:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.2">Zec 12:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.12.3">3</reference>). <div eID="gen24293" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12963"/><div sID="gen24294" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12963"/><hi type="bold">9. For--</hi>The blessed things promised in this and <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.10">Zep 3:10</reference> are the immediate results of the punishment inflicted on the nations, mentioned in <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.8">Zep 3:8</reference> (compare <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.19">Zep 3:19</reference>).<div eID="gen24294" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24295" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">turn to the people a pure language--</hi>that is, changing their impure language I will give to them again a pure language (literally, "lip"). Compare for this Hebrew idiom, <reference osisRef="1Sam.10.9">1Sa 10:9</reference>, Margin. The confusion of languages was of the penalty sin, probably idolatry at Babel (<reference osisRef="Gen.11.1-Gen.11.6">Ge 11:1-6</reference>, Margin, where also "lip" expresses language, and perhaps also religion; <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.4">Zep 3:4</reference>, "a tower whose top may reach unto heaven," or rather, points to heaven, namely, dedicated to the heavens idolized, or Bel); certainly, of rebellion against God's will. An earnest of the removal of this penalty was the gift of tongues on Pentecost (<reference osisRef="Acts.2.6-Acts.2.13">Ac 2:6-13</reference>). The full restoration of the earth's unity of language and of worship is yet future, and is connected with the restoration of the Jews, to be followed by the conversion of the world. Compare <reference osisRef="Isa.19.18">Is 19:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.9">Zec 14:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.15.6">Ro 15:6</reference>, "with one mind and one mouth glorify God." The Gentiles' lips have been rendered impure through being the instruments of calling on idols and dishonoring God (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.16.4">Psa 16:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.2.17">Ho 2:17</reference>). Whether Hebrew shall be the one universal language or not, the God of the Hebrews shall be the one only object of worship. Until the Holy Ghost purify the lips, we cannot rightly call upon God (<reference osisRef="Isa.6.5-Isa.6.7">Is 6:5-7</reference>).<div eID="gen24295" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24296" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">serve him with one consent--</hi>literally, "shoulder" or "back"; metaphor from a yoke, or burden, borne between two (<reference osisRef="Num.13.23">Nu 13:23</reference>); helping one another with conjoint effort. If one of the two bearers of a burden, laid on both conjointly, give way, the burden must fall to the earth [Calvin]. Christ's rule is called a burden (<reference osisRef="Matt.11.30">Mt 11:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.15.28">Ac 15:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.2.24">Re 2:24</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="2Cor.6.14">2Co 6:14</reference> for the same image). <div eID="gen24296" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12964"/><div sID="gen24297" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12964"/><hi type="bold">10. From beyond ... Ethiopia my suppliants--</hi>literally, "burners of incense" (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.141.2">Psa 141:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.5.8">Re 5:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.8.3">8:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.8.4">4</reference>). The Israelites are meant, called "the daughter of My dispersed," a Hebrew idiom for My dispersed people. "The rivers of Ethiopia" are those which enclose it on the north. In the west of Abyssinia there has long existed a people called Falashas, or "emigrants" (akin to the synonym "Philistine"). These trace their origin to Palestine and profess the Jewish religion. In physical traits they resemble the Arabs. When Bruce was there, they had a Jewish king, Gideon, and his queen, Judith. Probably the Abyssinian Christians were originally in part converted Jews. They are here made the representatives of all Israel which is to be restored.<div eID="gen24297" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24298" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall bring mine offering--</hi>that is, the offering that is My right. I prefer, with De Wette and Chaldee Version, making "suppliants" the objective case, not the nominative. The peoples: (<reference osisRef="Zeph.3.8">Zep 3:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.9">9</reference>), brought to fear Me by My judgments, "shall bring as Mine offering My suppliants (an appropriate term for the Jews, on whom then there shall have been poured the spirit of supplications, <reference osisRef="Zech.12.10">Zec 12:10</reference>), the daughter of My dispersed." So <reference osisRef="Isa.66.20">Is 66:20</reference>, "they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the Lord." Compare Horsley's view of <reference osisRef="Isa.18.1">Is 18:1</reference>, 2, 7. England in this view may be the naval power to restore Israel to Palestine (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.9">Is 60:9</reference>). The Hebrew for "Ethiopia" is Cush, which may include not only Ethiopia, but also the region of the Tigris and Babylon, where Nimrod, Cush's son (<reference osisRef="Gen.10.8-Gen.10.12">Ge 10:8-12</reference>), founded Nineveh and acquired Babylon, and where the ten tribes are mentioned as being scattered (<reference osisRef="1Pet.1.1">1Pe 1:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.5.13">5:13</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Isa.11.11">Is 11:11</reference>). entries.content_plain: 10. From beyond ... Ethiopia my suppliants-- literally, "burners of incense" (compare Psa 141:2 ; Re 5:8 ; 8:3 , 4 ). The Israelites are meant, called "the daughter of My dispersed," a Hebrew idiom for My dispersed people. "The rivers of Ethiopia" are those which enclose it on the north. In the west of Abyssinia there has long existed a people called Falashas, or "emigrants" (akin to the synonym "Philistine"). These trace their origin to Palestine and profess the Jewish religion. In physical traits they resemble the Arabs. When Bruce was there, they had a Jewish king, Gideon, and his queen, Judith. Probably the Abyssinian Christians were originally in part converted Jews. They are here made the representatives of all Israel which is to be restored. shall bring mine offering-- that is, the offering that is My right. I prefer, with De Wette and Chaldee Version, making "suppliants" the objective case, not the nominative. The peoples: ( Zep 3:8 , 9 ), brought to fear Me by My judgments, "shall bring as Mine offering My suppliants (an appropriate term for the Jews, on whom then there shall have been poured the spirit of supplications, Zec 12:10 ), the daughter of My dispersed." So Is 66:20 , "they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the Lord." Compare Horsley's view of Is 18:1 , 2, 7. The restoration under Cyrus of the Jews transported under Pharaoh-necho to Egypt and Ethiopia, was an earnest of the future restoration under Christ.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12971"/><div sID="gen24309" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12971"/><hi type="bold">17. he will rest in his love--</hi>content with it as His supreme delight (compare <reference osisRef="Luke.15.7">Lu 15:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Luke.15.10">10</reference>) [Calvin], (<reference osisRef="Isa.62.5">Is 62:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.65.19">65:19</reference>). Or, He shall be silent, namely as to thy faults, not imputing them to thee [Maurer] (<reference osisRef="Ps.32.2">Psa 32:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.33.16">Eze 33:16</reference>). I prefer explaining it of that calm silent joy in the possession of the object of one's love, too great for words to express: just as God after the six days of creation rested with silent satisfaction in His work, for "behold it was very good" (<reference osisRef="Gen.1.31">Ge 1:31</reference>; 2:2). So the parallel clause by contrast expresses the joy, not kept silent as this, but uttered in "singing." <div eID="gen24309" type="x-p"/>
